newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel sees progress on NATO-Russia talks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel sees progress on NATO-Russia talks - paper.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said a NATO-Russia deal over the Alliance's eastward expansion had made more progress than "generally accepted", the Welt am Sonntag newspaper reported on Sunday.

Kinkel's remarks came ahead of a meeting in Moscow on Sunday between NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov to draw up a single draft document mapping out their new post-Cold War relationship.

Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Yeltsin's closest ally in the West, and other North Atlantic Treaty Organisation leaders have said Russia cannot veto NATO's enlargement, but they hope to reach an agreement with Russia on the expansion proposals.

Several senior alliance sources say there are still big differences with Moscow and no breakthrough would emerge from Sunday's exchange, but recent signs showed the Russians now wanted to deal, even if the price they are asking is too high.
But Kinkel said the Alliance had made more progress in persuading Russia to accept it plans to take in former Warsaw Pact allies in eastern Europe "than generally accepted".
"The matter is now under way," the paper quoted him as saying.

Kinkel, who has met Primakov seven times over the last year in a diplomatic offensive to persuade to make NATO's plans more palatable to Russia, said he expected "three or four countries" to join in the first round of new NATO members.
"The aim is to take them in by 1999," it quoted Kinkel as saying. Germany is Russia's closest ally in the West and is playing an important diplomatic role in helping to negotiate a deal with Moscow.

Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to invited to join at a NATO summit in Madrid in July. The United States supports Slovenia's bid as a possible fourth candidate as a bridge between Hungary and Italy, while France and Italy are keen on Romania to strengthen the southern European axis.
Citing western diplomats, the newspaper said Russia was expected to agree to a charta on cooperation with NATO envisaging a NATO-Russia council on which Russia would have equal status with NATO.

Senior aides of Solana and Primakov have been working in Moscow over the last week preparing the ground for Sunday's meeting after Primakov handed over several draft texts on different aspects of a deal in Brussels two weeks ago.
